title: Letting prototypes become production systems without a governed path
summary: Give non-technical builders a supported route from useful experiment to owned, tested service.
diagnosis: The danger is not that a subject-matter expert creates a useful prototype. It is that a prototype gains users, permissions and business importance without a deliberate promotion decision. A production service needs someone who can explain its dependencies, evaluate changes, handle incidents and support users—even when AI generated much of the implementation.
diagnostic_questions: Where is the boundary between a private experiment, a shared pilot and a production dependency?
Who can approve promotion, and what evidence must they inspect?
Can the system be rebuilt, supported and stopped without the original creator’s personal account?
proposed_actions: Offer a sandbox and an approved promotion path with increasing controls as users, sensitivity and action authority grow.
Require representative tests, named owners, service identities, versioned artifacts, support arrangements and recovery evidence before production use.
Let business experts own intent and acceptance examples while involving engineering and risk specialists where the responsibility requires their skills.
working_artifact: Promotion dossier: intended users; purpose; version; data and permissions; tests and results; limitations; reviewer; operating owner; dependencies; monitoring; recovery procedure; support route; release decision.
measures: Share of shared applications with an explicit lifecycle stage and production owner.
Time from a useful prototype to a properly supported release, including the reasons for delay.
Incidents, unsupported usage and abandoned applications after rollout—not simply the count of citizen-built apps.
tradeoff: A heavy process for every experiment will encourage bypasses. Scale the requirements to the application’s reach and consequences, but keep the transition visible. Clear Markdown specifications help; they do not replace production engineering or access enforcement.
illustrative_case: Illustrative application: a planner’s private spreadsheet assistant becomes a team application only after its data scope, output checks, support owner and deployment account are approved. The useful prototype is preserved, not silently treated as a finished service.
